> The example labels below (a bakery, a parcel, a team) are filler. Copy the
> markup, never the content. Every label and number on a page must come from your
> sources.

Every diagram is HTML styled by `assets/template.html`. Each one sits in a figure:

```html
<figure class="fig">
  <p class="fig-title"><span>What this diagram shows</span></p>
  …one component…
  <p class="fig-note"><b>What to notice:</b> the one thing to look at.</p>
</figure>
```

The template fills in the stagger order (`--i`), item counts (`--n`) and angles
(`--a`) for you. Components respond to the **figure's** width, so a flow turns
vertical in a narrow column or on a phone. Keep labels to about six words; the prose
carries the nuance.

## Pick by the shape of the idea

| The idea is… | Use |
|---|---|
| a sequence of steps | flow (3 to 5 steps) or timeline (dated) |
| before and after, or what changed | versus titled "Before" / "After" (no `win`), or the same diagram twice, side by side |
| change over time | timeline (events) or columns (amounts) |
| commit history, or versions that split and join again | branches |
| networks, anything with crossing connections | a custom diagram (see "A diagram with no component" below) |
| a loop that repeats | cycle (3 to 6 nodes) |
| two options compared | versus |
| amounts compared | bars (horizontal), columns (a few values over time) |
| parts of a whole | split |
| who gets how far, or what shrinks | layers |
| layers of a system | stack (or, in full mode, an exploded view) |
| one thing in the middle, many around it | hub |
| a hierarchy | tree (one level of children) |
| two factors that sort things into four groups | matrix |
| where something sits on a range, or a threshold | scale |
| a few headline numbers | stats |
| messages between parties | sequence |

Colour: grey by default; add `hi` to the one item that matters (orange) and
`strong` for a dark emphasis. Use colour to mean something, never to decorate.
Text placed on an orange, green or red fill uses `var(--on-accent)`.

## Flow

```html
<div class="d-flow">
  <div class="fl-step"><span class="fl-dot">1</span><b>Mix</b><span>flour, water, salt</span></div>
  <div class="fl-step"><span class="fl-dot"><svg class="ic"><use href="#i-clock"/></svg></span><b>Rest</b><span>12 hours</span></div>
  <div class="fl-step"><span class="fl-dot">3</span><b>Bake</b><span>40 minutes</span></div>
</div>
```

The line draws left to right, then each step rises in turn. Put a number or an icon
in `.fl-dot`. Vertical on narrow widths.

## Cycle

```html
<div class="d-cycle">
  <div class="cy-ring"></div><div class="cy-orbit"></div>
  <div class="cy-center">one loop<br>per order</div>
  <div class="cy-node"><b>Order</b>a customer asks</div>
  <div class="cy-node"><b>Bake</b>the kitchen makes it</div>
  <div class="cy-node"><b>Deliver</b>it arrives</div>
  <div class="cy-node"><b>Review</b>feedback shapes the next</div>
</div>
```

Nodes spread evenly from the top, clockwise. A dot travels the ring twice. It
becomes a plain list on narrow widths.

## Versus

```html
<div class="d-versus">
  <div class="vs-col"><h3><svg class="ic"><use href="#i-circle-x"/></svg>Option A</h3><ul><li>Point</li><li>Point</li></ul></div>
  <div class="vs-col win"><h3><svg class="ic"><use href="#i-circle-check"/></svg>Option B</h3><ul><li>Point</li><li>Point</li></ul></div>
</div>
```

`win` marks the side your sources recommend; leave it off when they don't
recommend one, and for before/after comparisons. Keep the rows parallel: the same
question answered on both sides, in the same order. Rows line up across the two
columns even when one side wraps.

## Bars (horizontal)

```html
<div class="d-bars">
  <div class="bar-row"><span class="lab">Bakery A<small>city centre</small></span><span class="bar-track"><span class="bar" style="--to:92"></span></span><span class="val">920</span></div>
  <div class="bar-row hi"><span class="lab">Bakery B</span><span class="bar-track"><span class="bar" style="--to:64"></span></span><span class="val">640</span></div>
</div>
```

`--to` is the bar's end as a percentage of the track. Scale it yourself:
`value / max × 100`, rounded. **Bar lengths must be proportional to the real
numbers**: check the arithmetic. Negative values: add `has-zero` to `.d-bars`, set
`--zero` (where 0 sits, as a percentage) on it, give negative rows class `neg`, and
use `--from` (where the bar starts) and `--to` (where it ends).

```html
<div class="d-bars has-zero" style="--zero:20">
  <div class="bar-row"><span class="lab">Gain</span><span class="bar-track"><span class="bar" style="--from:20;--to:48"></span></span><span class="val">0.70</span></div>
  <div class="bar-row neg hi"><span class="lab">Loss</span><span class="bar-track"><span class="bar" style="--from:6.8;--to:20"></span></span><span class="val">−0.33</span></div>
</div>
```

## Columns (vertical)

```html
<div class="d-columns">
  <div class="col"><span class="v">12</span><i style="--h:40"></i></div>
  <div class="col"><span class="v">21</span><i style="--h:70"></i></div>
  <div class="col hi"><span class="v">30</span><i style="--h:100"></i></div>
</div>
<div class="cols-labels"><span>2024</span><span>2025</span><span>2026</span></div>
```

`--h` is the height as a percentage of the tallest column. Use up to about eight
columns.

## Split (parts of a whole)

```html
<div class="d-split"><span class="hi" style="--w:55">55%</span><span style="--w:30">30%</span><span class="s2" style="--w:15"></span></div>
<div class="split-legend"><span style="--c:var(--accent)">Rent</span><span style="--c:var(--series)">Staff</span><span style="--c:var(--series-2)">Flour</span></div>
```

The `--w` values must add up to 100. Leave the text out of segments narrower than
about 12.

## Layers (who gets how far)

```html
<div class="d-layers">
  <div class="ly hi"><div class="ly-t"><b>The short version</b><span>everyone</span></div><span class="ly-line" style="--w:100"></span></div>
  <div class="ly"><div class="ly-t"><b>How it works</b><span>most readers</span></div><span class="ly-line" style="--w:66"></span></div>
  <div class="ly"><div class="ly-t"><b>Deep dive</b><span>the curious</span></div><span class="ly-line" style="--w:34"></span></div>
</div>
```

## Stack (layers of a system)

```html
<div class="d-stack">
  <div class="st-layer"><svg class="ic"><use href="#i-monitor"/></svg><div><b>Website</b><span>what customers see</span></div><span class="tag">front end</span></div>
  <div class="st-layer hi"><svg class="ic"><use href="#i-server"/></svg><div><b>Order service</b><span>checks and stores orders</span></div><span class="tag">back end</span></div>
  <div class="st-layer"><svg class="ic"><use href="#i-database"/></svg><div><b>Database</b><span>keeps every order</span></div><span class="tag">storage</span></div>
</div>
```

Top to bottom: closest to the user first.

## Timeline

```html
<div class="d-timeline">
  <div class="tl-item"><span class="tl-when">March</span><span class="tl-dot"></span><b>Plan</b><span>scope agreed</span></div>
  <div class="tl-item hi"><span class="tl-when">June</span><span class="tl-dot"></span><b>Launch</b><span>first customers</span></div>
  <div class="tl-item"><span class="tl-when">October</span><span class="tl-dot"></span><b>Review</b><span>keep or change</span></div>
</div>
```

Use three to six items. It turns vertical on narrow widths.

## Hub

```html
<div class="d-hub">
  <div class="hub-core">Order service</div>
  <span class="hub-spoke"></span><span class="hub-spoke"></span><span class="hub-spoke"></span><span class="hub-spoke"></span>
  <div class="hub-node"><b>Website</b>places orders</div>
  <div class="hub-node"><b>Kitchen</b>gets tickets</div>
  <div class="hub-node"><b>Payments</b>takes money</div>
  <div class="hub-node"><b>Drivers</b>get routes</div>
</div>
```

Use one spoke per node, and four to eight nodes.

## Tree

```html
<div class="d-tree">
  <div class="tr-root">Company</div>
  <div class="tr-kids">
    <div class="tr-kid"><b>Sales</b>finds customers</div>
    <div class="tr-kid"><b>Kitchen</b>makes the product</div>
    <div class="tr-kid"><b>Delivery</b>gets it there</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Matrix (2 × 2)

```html
<div class="d-matrix">
  <span class="mx-y">more effort →</span>
  <div class="mx-cell"><b>Plan it</b>big win, big effort</div>
  <div class="mx-cell"><b>Avoid</b>small win, big effort</div>
  <div class="mx-cell hi"><b>Do now</b>big win, little effort</div>
  <div class="mx-cell"><b>Maybe</b>small win, little effort</div>
  <span class="mx-x">more value →</span>
</div>
```

The cells fill row by row: top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right.

## Scale (position on a range)

```html
<div class="d-scale">
  <span class="sc-axis"></span>
  <span class="sc-zone" style="--from:70;--to:100"></span>
  <span class="sc-mark" style="--v:82"><span>this year: 82</span></span>
  <span class="sc-tick start" style="--v:0">0</span><span class="sc-tick" style="--v:70">danger above 70</span><span class="sc-tick end" style="--v:100">100</span>
</div>
```

## Branches (commit history)

For git history, or any versions that split off and join again. The grid has a
column per moment and a row per branch; commits are dots, `br-line` runs along a
row, and `br-link` draws the elbow where a branch splits off (`fork`) or joins
(`join`). The upper row's number is `--r`, the lower row's `--r2`.

```html
<div class="d-branches" style="--cols:5; --rows:2">
  <span class="br-name" style="--r:1">main</span>
  <span class="br-name" style="--r:2">feature</span>
  <span class="br-line" style="--r:1; --from:1; --to:5; --i:0"></span>
  <span class="br-link fork mine" style="--r:1; --r2:2; --from:2; --to:3; --i:1"></span>
  <span class="br-line mine" style="--r:2; --from:3; --to:4; --i:1"></span>
  <span class="br-link join mine" style="--r:1; --r2:2; --from:4; --to:5; --i:2"></span>
  <span class="br-c" style="--r:1; --c:1; --i:0">A</span>
  <span class="br-c" style="--r:1; --c:2; --i:0">B</span>
  <span class="br-c mine" style="--r:2; --c:3; --i:1">C</span>
  <span class="br-c mine" style="--r:2; --c:4; --i:1">D</span>
  <span class="br-c hi" style="--r:1; --c:5; --i:2">M</span>
</div>
```

After a rebase, the old commits stay as dashed `ghost`s and the copies sit at the
end of the straight line:

```html
<div class="d-branches" style="--cols:6; --rows:2">
  <span class="br-name" style="--r:1">main</span>
  <span class="br-name" style="--r:2">before</span>
  <span class="br-line" style="--r:1; --from:1; --to:6; --i:0"></span>
  <span class="br-link fork ghost" style="--r:1; --r2:2; --from:2; --to:3; --i:0"></span>
  <span class="br-line ghost" style="--r:2; --from:3; --to:4; --i:0"></span>
  <span class="br-c" style="--r:1; --c:1; --i:0">A</span>
  <span class="br-c" style="--r:1; --c:2; --i:0">B</span>
  <span class="br-c ghost" style="--r:2; --c:3; --i:0">C</span>
  <span class="br-c ghost" style="--r:2; --c:4; --i:0">D</span>
  <span class="br-c" style="--r:1; --c:3; --i:1">X</span>
  <span class="br-c" style="--r:1; --c:4; --i:1">Y</span>
  <span class="br-c mine" style="--r:1; --c:5; --i:2">C′</span>
  <span class="br-c hi" style="--r:1; --c:6; --i:2">D′</span>
</div>
```

`mine` marks the reader's own commits (orange outline), `hi` the one commit to look
at, `ghost` commits that no longer count. Set `--i` yourself, one beat per step of
the story (here: history, the branch, the merge). Keep to about seven columns, so
the dots fit on a phone, and use one or two letters per commit: the prose names
them. Two diagrams side by side ("before" and "after") read better than one dense one.

## Stats

```html
<div class="d-stats">
  <div class="stat"><span class="num">3</span><span>bakeries</span></div>
  <div class="stat hi"><span class="num"><span class="count" style="--to:920"></span></span><span>orders a day</span></div>
  <div class="stat"><span class="num">40 min</span><span>average delivery</span></div>
</div>
```

`.count` counts up to `--to` (whole numbers only). Write units outside it.

## Sequence (messages between parties)

```html
<div class="d-seq" style="--lanes:3">
  <div class="seq-actors">
    <div class="seq-actor"><span class="disc"><svg class="ic"><use href="#i-user"/></svg></span><b>Customer</b><small>on the website</small></div>
    <div class="seq-actor"><span class="disc"><svg class="ic"><use href="#i-server"/></svg></span><b>Shop</b></div>
    <div class="seq-actor"><span class="disc"><svg class="ic"><use href="#i-credit-card"/></svg></span><b>Bank</b></div>
  </div>
  <div class="seq-rows">
    <div class="msg" style="--a:0;--b:1"><span class="line"></span><span class="lbl">place order</span><span class="pkt">order</span></div>
    <div class="msg direct" style="--a:1;--b:2"><span class="line"></span><span class="lbl">charge the card</span><span class="pkt">£12</span></div>
    <div class="msg secret" style="--a:2;--b:1"><span class="line"></span><span class="lbl">approved</span><span class="pkt">ok</span></div>
  </div>
  <div class="seq-legend"><span>through the customer's browser</span><span class="solid">direct</span></div>
</div>
```

`--a` and `--b` are the sending and receiving lanes, counted from 0 at the left.
Lines are dashed by default; `direct` makes them solid; `secret` makes the packet
dark (for passwords, keys, money). Here every row shows at once. To play it step by
step, put it in a Show me walkthrough or a scroll story with `data-at` on each row
(showme.md). Up to four lanes fit on a phone.

## Supporting pieces

- **Analogy**, inside `.text`: `<div class="analogy">A hotel key card opens your room, not every room…</div>`
- **Callout**: `<div class="callout"><svg class="ic"><use href="#i-info"/></svg><div>Text.</div></div>` (`callout warn` for cautions).
## A diagram with no component

Some ideas need their own drawing: commit history with branches, a network, a
floor plan. Build it in `custom.css`:

- **Shapes** are elements: circles (`border-radius: 50%`), boxes, and labels in
  `<span>`s. Lay them out with grid or flex, not absolute pixel positions, so they
  survive a phone width. Wrap the drawing in `.fig` and use container queries
  (`@container (max-width: 480px)`) for the narrow version.
- **Connectors**: straight lines are borders or thin elements (`height: 1.5px;
  background: var(--line)`); an elbow is a box with two borders and a rounded
  corner. Inline SVG is allowed for curves CSS can't draw: use `stroke="currentColor"`
  or `style="stroke: var(--line)"`, never fixed colours.
- **Colours** come only from the variables (`--accent`, `--strong`, `--series`,
  `--series-2`, `--line`, `--muted`, `--on-accent`); the build warns about raw
  colours. Dashed or faded (`opacity: .4`) shapes mean "before" or "gone".
- **Size**: as many elements as the idea needs, but group them so the eye sees
  three to seven chunks (for example, two branches of five commits each).
- **Motion**: use the template's keyframes (`rise`, `fade`, `pop`, `grow-x`,
  `grow-y`), paced for reading and scaled by the pace:
  `animation: rise calc(.8s * var(--tempo)) var(--ease) both;
  animation-delay: calc((var(--i) * var(--beat) + 200ms) * var(--tempo));`.
  Use `--beat` between labelled elements (commits with names, boxes with text) and
  `--stagger` between unlabelled marks. The template fills in `--i` only for its own
  components, so set `style="--i:0"`, `--i:1`… on your elements, in the order
  you'd explain them. Group elements that belong together (one branch, one row)
  under the same `--i`, so a 13-element drawing plays in four or five readable beats.
  The easy way: add `class="paced"` and `style="--i:N"` to each element and write
  no delays at all. If you do write `animation-delay`, declare it **after** any
  `animation:` shorthand that applies to the same elements: the shorthand resets
  the delay to zero, and the whole drawing appears at once.
